newsitem.title: UK: Invesco sets fund merger with AIM Management.
newsitem.headline: Invesco sets fund merger with AIM Management.

text.p: Britain's Invesco Plc said Monday it planned to merge with AIM Manangement Group Inc., one of the largest and fastest-growing mutual fund managers in the United States, to create a group with funds under management in excess of 90 billion pounds ($147 billion).
Invesco will take a majority holding in an enlarged group to be renamed AMVESCO Plc, Invesco said. AIM was valued at about $1.6 billion.

Invesco will issue 290 million new shares, valued at about $1.1 billion, to the existing holders of AIM shares. The balance of the consideration is to be in cash raised from a combination of debt and a proposed one-for-five rights issue.

AIM shareholders will own about 45 percent of the enlarged group, and Invesco said it believed that in the 1997 financial year the merger would have a "broadly neutral" impact on Invesco's earnings per share.

"AMVESCO will be a major investment management company with the scale necessary for success as a financially strong and independent business, operating in an increasingly concentrated industry," Charles Brady, chairman and chief executive of Invesco, said in a statement announcing the deal.
"This strategic merger will strengthen both companies and, at the same time, preserve our independent cultures which have been so essential to our success," AIM Chief Executive Charles Bauer added.
